title: Graceful Capacity Degradation: Commercialization and Customer Onboarding Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the product, commercial, and operational approach for "graceful capacity degradation" — an end-to-end feature that lets Redwood continue serving customer traffic under transient capacity pressure by: routing to lower-fidelity model variants, applying short-term batching changes, and issuing customer-facing credits where quality/latency SLOs are impacted. The goal is to keep customer applications online while limiting cost and preserving predictable economics.

Use cases:
- Enterprise customers on Dedicated pools experiencing regional GPU contention.
- Hosted-tier customers during cross-region failover events.
- Migration windows where full-capacity variants are being rolled out.

Who should read this: product managers, solutions engineering, account teams, SRE, billing, and customer success.

Objectives

1) Business: minimize revenue churn from outages by providing a transparent, contractual fallback behavior and straightforward crediting model.
2) Product: expose controls for fidelity vs cost tradeoffs and automated fallback policies per tenant.
3) Ops: give SREs deterministic, observable fallbacks with clear telemetry and rollback procedures.

Scope and Non-Scope

In scope:
- Policy definitions in the control plane for per-tenant fallback sequencing (model variant, quantization, batching).
- Billing credit calculation for short-term fidelity/latency degradations.
- Customer onboarding flows and contract language templates.
- Console UX for visualizing fallback events and credit history.

Out of scope:
- Long-term contract renegotiation (handled by Sales).
- Deep model retraining to recover fidelity (handled by Applied ML).

Product contract and SLO implications

SLO mapping (examples):
- Availability SLO: 99.95% regional for Hosted API (unchanged).
- Latency SLO (TR1 route): p95 < 300ms. During graceful degradation that target may be relaxed to p95 < 700ms per policy.
- Quality SLO: BLEU/ROUGE or embedding distance budget for evaluated prompt sets — a soft guard used to trigger crediting when exceeded.

When a degradation policy is applied, the system will:
1) Record an event in routing-proxy and console (event_id).
2) Flag the tenant for billing-service credit evaluation.
3) Update runtime headers to indicate fallback variant (X-Redwood-Fallback-Variant).

Credit calculation rules (summary):
- Windowed approach: credits are calculated per 5-minute window where observed quality/latency exceeds the configured tenant thresholds.
- Credit basis: fraction of token cost attributable to degraded fidelity + fixed service-level goodwill amount.
- Max credit cap: 20% of the tenant’s billed usage in the affected week unless escalated by CSM.

Operational controls and owner ship

Owners: 
- Product: Aisha Patel (owner for commercial playbook updates)
- Opt-in policy feature flag: eng-platform (feature-flag service)
- Runtime/fallback orchestration: eng-serving-runtime (runtime team)
- Billing & credits engine: finance-and-legal (billing-service team)
- Onboarding & comms: customer-success-and-support (CSM team)

Immediate contacts (escalation):
- Oncall SRE: see /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-rotations
- Billing escalation: Sana Becker (finance)

Customer onboarding checklist (CSM / Solutions Eng)

1) Pre-signing (Contract/Legal):
   - Insert fallback covenant into Appendix B of the contract (template snippet below).
   - Agree on maximum weekly credit cap and SLA tiers.

2) Initial setup (first 7 days):
   - Enable per-tenant fallback policy default in the Console (DefaultPolicy: standard_fallback_v1).
   - Capture a canonical prompt set (10–20 prompts) for quality monitoring. Add to tenant profile: 'fallback_guard_prompts'.
   - Set tenant-specific thresholds: latency_margin_ms, embedding_distance_threshold.

3) Post-activation (day 7–30):
   - Run a simulated load test using the hosted-sim-runner to validate fallback behavior.
   - Walk through customer Console views showing fallback events and credits.
   - Schedule a QBR within first 30 days to review observed fallbacks and crediting.

Template contract snippet (Appendix B):

"During transient capacity constraints Redwood may route traffic to lower-fidelity model variants or apply batching that can affect latency and output characteristics. Redwood will provide usage credits for material degradations consistent with the Customer’s SLA. The maximum weekly credit is 20% of billed usage for the affected time period unless otherwise negotiated."

Staged rollout plan (recommended)

1) Canary (internal): enable on 10 internal tenants and exercise 3 failure modes (GPU pressure, cross-region network spike, warm-pool exhaustion). Duration: 2 weeks.
2) Beta (select customers): opt-in by invitation to up to 20 paying customers. Monitor for false positives in crediting and UX clarity. Duration: 4 weeks.
3) General availability: automatic opt-in default for new enterprise customers, opt-out for legacy contracts.

Rollout metrics to validate at each stage:
- False positive credit events per 1000 degraded windows < 1.
- Time to detect and apply fallback < 15s from threshold breach.
- Percentage of requests served without failover increased vs baseline (resilience uplift).

Billing and pricing impact examples (table)

| Degradation Level | Runtime change | Billing credit % (windowed) | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Minor | small-quant (int8) | 5% | Quality delta within 3% of baseline on eval prompts |
| Moderate | reduced-fp32-context | 12% | p95 latency > baseline by +300ms OR embedding distance exceedance |
| Major | variant-fallback-to-small | 20% (cap) | Significant quality regression; automatic CSM review triggered |

Example credit calculation (simplified):
- Tenant A had $2,000 billed in the affected week. During a 30-minute incident with moderate degradations affecting 3 five-minute windows, system calculates 12% credit on tokens for those windows: estimated credit = $2,000 * (minutes_affected / total_week_minutes) * 12% (simplified). Final credits are rounded and shown in Console adjustments.

Console UX and telemetry requirements

Required Console elements: 
- Fallback events timeline per-tenant with event_id and reason codes (REASON_GPU_PRESSURE, REASON_COLD_START, REASON_NETWORK_EGRESS).
- Credit calculator preview and audit trail.
- Toggle for opt-in/out and tenant-specific thresholds.

Telemetry and logging:
- routing-proxy: fallback_applied (bool), fallback_variant (string), event_id (uuid).
- runtime-metrics: model_variant, avg_batch_size, effective_qps.
- billing-service: credit_eval_id, credit_amount, reason_code.

Operational runbook (SRE)

Trigger conditions: automated detection when any of the following repeat for N=3 consecutive 1-minute windows:
1) p95 latency > 2x configured latency SLO.
2) evaluated prompt-set quality metric breaches threshold.
3) GPU pool capacity utilization > 92% and queue depth > 50%

Immediate actions (ordered):
1) Confirm detection in routing-proxy and surface to incident channel #fallback-events.
2) If automated policy applied: verify X-Redwood-Fallback-Variant in live requests.
3) Notify oncall and CSM if predicted credit > $5,000 in the next 60 minutes.
4) If false-positive: rollback policy via feature-flag (feature-flag service CLI).

CLI snippets (example):

# Inspect current fallback policy for tenant
redwoodctl tenants get --id tenant_123 --fields fallback_policy

# Force-rollout rollback (engineering only)
redwoodctl feature-flags set graceful_degradation false --scope tenant_123 --reason "false-positive"

Acceptance criteria for GA

- Feature flagged and controllable per-tenant in Console.
- Billing-service integration able to generate provisional credits and surface to Console.
- Automated detection rules validated with < 1% false positives in Beta.
- CSM & Sales trained with playbook and contract template.

Success metrics (product & commercial)

- Reduction in outage-related churn rate by 30% for customers using fallback within 6 months.
- Mean time to apply fallback < 15s.
- Percentage of fallback events with customer-visible credits processed within 24 hours > 95%.

Risks and mitigations

Risk: Customers perceive credits as a license for degraded experience.
Mitigation: Restrict rollout to enterprise customers by default; add explicit contract language and weekly credit caps.

Risk: Over-crediting due to noisy quality signals.
Mitigation: Require N=3 consecutive windows and cross-validate with canonical prompt-set before issuing credits.

Appendix: Implementation notes for eng teams

- routing-proxy should emit structured event payloads to kafka topic: fallback-events (schema v1). Fields: event_id, tenant_id, reason_code, variant, window_start, window_end.
- billing-service will consume fallback-events and join with usage-aggregates to produce provisional credit entries (credit_eval_id).
- Console will render a reversible audit trail entry for each provisional credit and allow CSM to approve final credit posting.

Sample fallback-events kafka payload (human readable):
{
  "event_id": "evt-8f3a2",
  "tenant_id": "tenant_123",
  "reason_code": "REASON_GPU_PRESSURE",
  "variant": "small-variant-quantized-v2",
  "window": "2026-06-09T10:05:00Z/2026-06-09T10:10:00Z",
  "metrics": {"p95_latency_ms": 820, "embedding_distance_delta": 0.12}
}

Note: the actual kafka schema is managed in eng-platform/schemas and must be updated in the schema registry before GA.

Related pages and next steps

- Coordinate with finance-and-legal to finalize crediting algorithm and weekly caps.
- Schedule lab tests with Applied ML to calibrate canonical prompt-sets for Beta tenants.
- Run the Canary starting 2026-07-05 and record validation metrics in /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite.
